about.title: Fairfax Medical Malpractice Claims
about.longDescription: Fairfax residents rely on nearby Marin County clinics and hospitals for care, and most visits go as expected. But when a diagnosis is missed, a surgery goes wrong, or medication is mishandled, the harm can be serious and lasting. California's medical malpractice laws are notably strict compared to other injury claims — tight filing windows, a required pre-suit notice, and a cap on non-economic damages all shape how these cases move forward. A small town like Fairfax means fewer local specialists, which can mean care was referred out to larger Marin or Bay Area facilities, adding another layer to sort out. If you believe a healthcare provider's error caused your injury, it helps to talk with someone who understands how these claims are evaluated. We handle medical malpractice claims and can review what happened, explain your options in plain terms, and help you understand next steps.

whyChoose.title: What Fairfax Patients Should Know About MICRA

items.title: Strict, Short Deadlines
items.desc: California generally requires malpractice claims within one year of discovering the injury, and never more than three years from when it occurred. Missing these windows can end a claim before it starts, so timing matters.

items.title: 90-Day Notice Requirement
items.desc: Before filing suit, California law requires giving the healthcare provider 90 days' advance notice. We can help make sure this step is handled correctly and doesn't jeopardize your claim.

items.title: Expert Review Is Usually Required
items.desc: A bad medical outcome by itself isn't proof of malpractice — California generally requires a qualified medical expert to support the claim. We can help arrange the kind of case evaluation this standard demands.

items.question: How long do I have to file a medical malpractice claim in Fairfax?
items.answer: Under California's MICRA rules, you generally have one year from when you discovered (or reasonably should have discovered) the injury, but never more than three years from the date it happened. These deadlines are strict and can vary by circumstance, so it's best to have us review your specific timeline as soon as possible.

items.question: Is there a limit on what I can recover for a malpractice injury?
items.answer: California caps non-economic damages, like pain and suffering, in medical malpractice cases, though the cap rises each year under current law. Economic damages, such as medical bills and lost income, are generally not subject to this cap. We can walk through how this applies to your situation.

items.question: I was treated at a clinic near Fairfax but the specialist was somewhere else in Marin County — does that change anything?
items.answer: It can add complexity, since more than one provider or facility may be involved in reviewing what happened. This doesn't prevent you from pursuing a claim, but it's exactly the kind of detail we should look at closely before any notice or filing occurs.

items.question: Does a bad outcome automatically mean malpractice occurred?
items.answer: No — California law requires more than just a disappointing result; it requires showing the provider failed to meet the accepted standard of care. That's why a qualified medical expert is almost always needed to support a claim. We can help determine whether your case has that kind of support.
